bounded_question: After the once decision 0x5f07490 runs on the owner object in 0x5f0e890, what does the resolver 0x5f074e0 called right after it do to pin owner+0xcb8 exactly once: which chain it walks, how the first non-canonical slot 0xc0 wins, when the value is installed, and what the call-site gate is?

callsite_0x5f0e890.gate: the helper and resolver run exactly when *(owner+0xc18) != 0 and not (*(owner+0xc60) != 0 and *(owner+0x30) != 0); the second combination jumps to 0x5f0f0a7 instead
callsite_0x5f0e890.object: r13, the owner-like object the hash-probe loop in 0x5f0e890 works on
callsite_0x5f0e890.sequence: call once helper 0x5f07490(r13), then call resolver 0x5f074e0(r13) on the same object

canonical_0x5d4b100.entry: called as a slot 0xc0 with (bool_out, node, value_out); it advances past the node it was called on first, because the caller already found that node's slot canonical
canonical_0x5d4b100.recursion: when the ninth level's slot is canonical too it is called and recurses into itself from the tenth node

dead_walk_finding.claim: two of the seven once-helper call sites never fire
dead_walk_finding.evidence: in 0x5fbcd50 the gate byte at frame+0x49 is set to 0 by the prologue (movb $0x0,0x49(%rsp)) and the walk is skipped while it is 0 (cmpb $0x0,0x49(%rsp); je); in 0x5fbcfa0 the same holds for frame+0x89. The only calls between the prologue and the gate are the 0x5fbbc40/0x5fbbc50 accessor and the 0x5fbba60 Status builder, neither of which writes the walker's stack frame, and the map headers at frame+0x78 / frame+0xb8 are never populated. The once-helper calls inside those two tree walks are therefore unreachable in every call path; the other five sites are live
dead_walk_finding.not_checked_this_cycle: reachability of the three sites in 0x5f0f930 was not checked; they are recorded as live by the absence of a dead gate, not by proof

got_canonical.second_slot_note: a second GOT slot also holds 0x5d4b100 by a RELATIVE record; no direct RIP-relative reader of 0x64cde48 was found in the linear disassembly, so its reader is an open unknown

sentinel_constant.meaning: 16 bytes installed at owner+0xcb8/+0xcc0 by the tail init: cb8 starts at -1 (unresolved), cc0 at 0

once_helper_0x5f07490.role: the once helper from #3304: it calls the predicate 0x5f07300 and latches owner+0xc68 to 1 with a lock cmpxchg only when the predicate returns true; re-shipped byte-identical from the RE-001-owner-tail-phases-115 packet

once_predicate_0x5f07300.role: the once predicate from #3304: it calls SkipListRep slot 15 (0x6062fb0) on both products and decides the shared-table resize from the 0.6 factor; re-shipped byte-identical from the RE-001-owner-tail-phases-115 packet

resolver_0x5f074e0.bool_gate: when the bool at rsp+0x10 is nonzero the value is NOT installed; when it is zero the value is installed
resolver_0x5f074e0.chain_link: each node links to the next through its +0x20 field
resolver_0x5f074e0.entry: owner+0xcb8 is read first; when it is not -1 the resolver returns at once and installs nothing
resolver_0x5f074e0.fifth_level: the fifth level's slot 0xc0 is called unconditionally; when it is the canonical 0x5d4b100 that function continues the walk
resolver_0x5f074e0.install: lock cmpxchg installs *(rsp+0x08) into owner+0xcb8 only when it is still -1
resolver_0x5f074e0.owned_free: the owned pointer at rsp+0x18, when non-null, is freed with delete[] (_ZdaPv) whether or not the value was installed
resolver_0x5f074e0.sentinel: owner+0xcb8 starts at -1, the low qword of the 16-byte constant at 0x456590 installed by the owner-tail init in #3304
resolver_0x5f074e0.slot: each node's vtable slot 0xc0, compared against the canonical resolver 0x5d4b100 held in GOT slot 0x64ed3e8
resolver_0x5f074e0.slot_call: the winning slot is called with (bool_out at rsp+0x10, node, value_out at rsp+0x08); the callee also provides the owned heap pointer read at rsp+0x18
